text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your shortness of breath and massive abdominal girth, we must determine if this is due to a large ascites or a lung issue. Please tell me: Is your breathing worse when you lie down, and have you noticed any leg swelling?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound, Chest X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with Malignant Ascites. Based on your age, nulliparity, large ovarian mass, increasing abdominal girth, and shortness of breath consistent with malignant ascites compressing the diaphragm, this is the most likely clinical picture. The normal CA-125 and lack of weight loss do not rule out this diagnosis, especially given the physical findings. I recommend proceeding immediately with a diagnostic paracentesis and CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to confirm the presence of malignant cells and stage the disease.
